title: Quebec Independence Movement Update — Oct 17, 2026
summary: The 59 Parti Québécois members were sworn in at the National Assembly, taking an oath to the people of Quebec rather than the King (outlets differ on Oct. 14 vs Oct. 15). A lawyer has asked the Superior Court to force members to swear allegiance to the King, seeking a ruling before the legislature reconvenes in mid-November. Premier-designate Paul St-Pierre Plamondon is due to present his cabinet on Oct. 21.

title: Quebec Independence Movement Update — Thu Oct 15, 2026
summary: 59 PQ members sworn in at National Assembly, oath to the people of Quebec rather than the King.

title: Quebec Independence Movement Update — Oct 11, 2026
summary: Premier-designate Paul St-Pierre Plamondon says the PQ will not swear an oath to the King and wants the Lieutenant-Governor kept out of the swearing-in; the exemption faces a legal challenge. PQ members are reportedly to be sworn in Oct. 15, with the cabinet to be announced Oct. 21. The PQ holds 59 of 127 seats, five short of a majority.

title: Breaking: New York Times analysis finds Quebec independence remains unlikely despite a rec
summary: New York Times analysis finds Quebec independence remains unlikely despite a recent Parti Québécois surge, with separatism driven more by cultural identity than a genuine push for a referendum.

title: Quebec Independence Movement Update — Oct 9, 2026
summary: Later counts put the Parti Québécois at about 59 of 127 seats on roughly 28% of the vote, with the Liberals at about 40 as Official Opposition. The CAQ lost all its seats. PM Mark Carney spoke with premier-designate Paul St-Pierre Plamondon and pledged cooperative federalism. The PQ will need opposition support to govern, and a referendum remains tied to Trump leaving office.

title: Quebec Independence Movement Update — Oct 7, 2026
summary: The Parti Québécois won the most seats on Oct 5 but fell short of a majority, at about 59 of 127 seats on under 30% of the vote. Paul St-Pierre Plamondon will lead a minority government. The Liberals and Conservatives say they will block any separation vote. The PQ has said a referendum will wait until after Trump leaves office in January 2029. Counts are preliminary.

title: Quebec Independence Movement Update — Tue Oct 6, 2026
summary: The secessionist Parti Québécois won the Quebec provincial election, promising a new referendum on Quebec's separation from Canada.
